rv.q: Nevertheless ‘The Majority’ – which is directed by David Overend and features some neat beehive projections by Mogzi Bromley-Morgans – is an admirably provocative piece of work.
It’s an impressive piece of solo performance, and, whenever you go, you’re guaranteed to get something you didn’t expect.
Yet this is a meandering piece, a shaggy-dog story that's politely thought-provoking but doesn't probe the inconsistencies it reveals.
A thought-provoking play but not as revealing as one had hoped.

But the flaw in his soft-liberal approach, which implies a moral equivalence between all forms of protest, is that it comes dangerously close to Trumpism and I can’t believe that is what Drummond would wish.
Light and entertaining as it is, The Majority is a bit too tricksy for my taste, and it is likely to remain a minority interest.
It’s all suitably entertaining, for sure, but I’m not sure it sparks as much debate as it could.
As it is, it’s an interesting curiosity.
Well, it's well staged, the performer is engaging and the keypads are fun, it's never boring but I'm not convinced it adds up to much more than that.

cn.t: An intriguing but flawed interactive exploration of democracy that entertains with its audience-voting gimmick, yet ultimately feels too tricksy and meandering to fully address the urgent political questions it raises.
